Rashi on Chullin 4b:10:1.hebrew: למעלה שאני - דאין אכילה לפניו, אבל אדם דצריך לאכילה, עיקר הסתה דידיה באכילה ושתיה:
Rashi on Chullin 4b:10:1.english: Incitement against the One on High is different - for there is no eating before Him; but a person, who needs food, the essence of his temptation is through eating and drinking.

Rashi on Chullin 4b:11:1.english: What is different about drinking - This is [part of] the answer [to the question, not a new question].

Rashi on Chullin 4b:1:1.hebrew: מותר מיד - ואע"ג דלא שהה כדי לאפות, דודאי עבר עליה הפסח, מותר לכשרים לאכול מחמצן מיד:
Rashi on Chullin 4b:1:1.english: Permitted immediately - Even though not enough time has passed for [new] baking, such that [this bread] certainly had Pesach pass over it, it is [nonetheless] permitted for kosher [Jews] to eat their leavened bread immediately.

Rashi on Chullin 4b:1:2.hebrew: מפני שהן מחליפין - בשל עובדי כוכבים, דכיון דמצי לאכול התירא דחמץ של עובד כוכבים שעבר עליו הפסח מותר, לא אכיל דידיה דחמץ של ישראל שעבר עליו הפסח אסור. ואע"ג דהשתא נמי איסור הוא לגביה, דהא מתהני מחמץ שעבר עליו הפסח, דאי לא דיהיב ליה לעובד כוכבים לא הוה יהיב ליה דידיה, אפ"ה כל מה דמצי למעבד בהיתירא פורתא עביד, ולדידן מיהא שרי, דאין לך איסור הנאה תופס חליפין חוץ מעבודת כוכבים והקדש ושביעית. וי"א שאף לעצמו מותר, וטעות הוא בידם, דא"כ מצינו דמים לחמץ בפסח ולשור הנסקל שאם רצה מוכרו לעובד כוכבים, ותנן האוכל תרומת חמץ בפסח פטור מן התשלומין ומדמי עצים:
Rashi on Chullin 4b:1:2.english: Because they exchange - [Their chametz] with that of idol-worshippers (non-Jews). Since he is able to eat the permitted one - that is, chametz belonging to a non-Jew over which Pesach passed, which is permitted - he does not eat his own, for chametz belonging to a Jew over which Pesach passed is forbidden. And even though now too it is, in a sense, forbidden to him, since he is benefiting from chametz over which Pesach passed - for had he not given his own [chametz] to the non-Jew, [the non-Jew] would not have given him his - nevertheless, whatever he is able to do in a permitted way, he does to some extent. And as far as we are concerned, in any case it is permitted, for there is no item forbidden for benefit that takes hold through exchange, except for idol worship, consecrated property (hekdesh), and produce of the sabbatical year (shevi'it). And some say that it is permitted even for himself, but this is a mistake on their part, for if so, we would find that chametz on Pesach has monetary value - like an ox condemned to be stoned, which he may sell to a non-Jew [and keep the proceeds] - yet we learned [in a mishnah]: one who eats terumah-chametz on Pesach is exempt from payment, even at the value of mere wood.

Rashi on Chullin 4b:2:1.english: (According to Rabbi) Yehuda - [This is stated] in the chapter "Kol Sha'ah" (Pesachim 28b).

Rashi on Chullin 4b:2:2.hebrew: איסור דאורייתא - ואע"ג דאורייתא היא, סמכינן אהחליפו:
Rashi on Chullin 4b:2:2.english: A Torah prohibition - Even though it is [a prohibition] of Torah law, we [nevertheless] rely on [the presumption that] he exchanged it.

Rashi on Chullin 4b:3:1.english: In [a matter] of Torah [law] we do not rule leniently - such as [in the case of] a carcass [that died without proper slaughter].

Rashi on Chullin 4b:4:1.hebrew: מי קתני שאני אומר החליפו - דהוי משמע דלא פשיטא לן דהחליפו, ואנן הוא דתלינן לקולא, משום דאיסור דרבנן הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 4b:4:1.english: Is it taught: "I say that they switched"? - For that wording would imply that it is not obvious to us that they switched, and that it is we who lean toward leniency, because it is [only] a rabbinic prohibition.

Rashi on Chullin 4b:4:2.hebrew: מפני שהן מחליפין קתני, דודאי מחליפין - וא"נ אוקמינן לה כר"ש, כ"ש דמסייע ליה טפי לרבא, דהשתא ומה בדרבנן דקילא איסורא ידעינן בהו, דהיכא דמשכח היתירא לא אכל איסורא דרבנן, כ"ש נבלה דאורייתא:
Rashi on Chullin 4b:4:2.english: "Because they get exchanged" is taught - that they certainly get exchanged - And even if we establish it in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, this supports Rava all the more. For now, in the case of a rabbinic prohibition, which is lenient, we know about them that wherever one finds a permitted [substitute], one does not eat the rabbinically forbidden [item] - all the more so [would one not eat] an unslaughtered carcass (neveilah), which is a Torah-level prohibition.

Rashi on Chullin 4b:5:1.english: Shall we say that [this] supports him - [supports] Rava.

Rashi on Chullin 4b:5:2.english: An apostate regarding [the prohibition of] orlah - He kicks against [i.e., scorns] this commandment.

Rashi on Chullin 4b:5:3.hebrew: לא הוי מומר לכל התורה כולה - ושחיט שפיר:
Rashi on Chullin 4b:5:3.english: He would not be an apostate with respect to the entire Torah - and he slaughters properly.

Rashi on Chullin 4b:6:1.hebrew: אי מומר לדבר אחר - למצוה אחרת דלא לשחיטה, ולא ראינוהו מומר לנבלות:
Rashi on Chullin 4b:6:1.english: If he is a transgressor concerning another matter - [meaning] concerning another mitzva, not concerning slaughtering, and we have not seen him being a transgressor with regard to [eating] unslaughtered animal carcasses.

Rashi on Chullin 4b:6:2.hebrew: לאותו דבר - לנבילות לתיאבון, ואיצטריך לאשמועינן דאפילו למצוה דחשיד עלה, כי מזמנין ליה היתירא, סמכינן עליה:
Rashi on Chullin 4b:6:2.english: To that same matter - [Meaning,] eating nevelot (unslaughtered carcasses) out of appetite. And it was necessary to teach us this: that even with regard to the very matter for which he is suspect, when he is offered permitted [food], we rely on him.

Rashi on Chullin 4b:7:1.hebrew: כהיתירא דמי ליה - וליכא למימר לא שביק היתירא ואכיל איסורא, דהא היתירא חשיב ליה:
Rashi on Chullin 4b:7:1.english: It is like a permitted act to him - And one cannot say [that he must be slaughtering properly because] he would not leave the permitted and eat the forbidden, since, after all, it is considered permitted to him [and so this reasoning does not apply to him].

Rashi on Chullin 4b:7:2.hebrew: אלא מומר - דקתני לעבודת כוכבים, ואיצטריך לאשמועינן משום דאמר מר: חמורה עבודת כוכבים, שכל הכופר בה כמודה בכל התורה כולה, ואפ"ה סמכינן עליה כרב ענן כו':
Rashi on Chullin 4b:7:2.english: Rather, a transgressor - for it teaches [the case of] a transgressor with regard to idol worship, and it was necessary to teach us this, because the master said: idol worship is severe, for whoever denies it is considered as one who affirms the entire Torah; and nevertheless we rely on him [that his slaughter is valid], in accordance with Rav Anan, etc.

Rashi on Chullin 4b:8:1.hebrew: אחאב וסיעתו חזינן בהו דעובדי עבודת כוכבים הוו, ובנבלה לא אשכחן בהו דפקרי, ואיכא למימר דיצרא דעבודת כוכבים תקיף עלייהו, ויהושפט צדיק גמור היה:
Rashi on Chullin 4b:8:1.english: Regarding Ahab and his company, we see about them that they were idol worshippers, but we do not find about them that they were brazen regarding [eating] a carcass (n'velah), and one can say that the inclination for idol worship was powerful over them, whereas Jehoshaphat was a completely righteous man.

Rashi on Chullin 4b:9:1.english: Slaughtered a sacrifice - [The Gemara means that] he assumed [Jehoshaphat] would eat [the sacrifice] with him.

Rashi on Chullin 4b:9:2.english: [He] did not actually eat - [i.e.,] Jehoshaphat.

Rashi on Chullin 4b:9:3.english: He incited him - to go up to Ramoth (to see) Gilead.

Tosafot on Chullin 4b:1:1.hebrew: מותר מיד מפני שהן מחליפין - פירוש מותר בהנאה למוכרו או להאכילו לפועלים עובדי כוכבים או לכלבים, אבל לישראל אסור באכילה, דגזרו על פתן של עובדי כוכבים. א"נ כדפירש ר"ת דבבצק איירי, דמותר באכילה, והשתא א"ש דלא תקשי היכי סברוה דאתיא כרבי יהודה, הא אית ליה בפ' כל שעה (פסחים דף כח:) דחמץ של עובד כוכבים שעבר עליו הפסח אסור בהנאה, אלא בבצק איירי, ומחלפי בבצק של עובדי כוכבים שלשו אחר הפסח, ומותר מיד דקאמר היינו כשיעור לישה. ומה שפירש בקונטרס שמרויחין, דלדידן מיהא שרי דאין תופס את דמיו, דדוקא לדידיה אסור שבא לו מחמת חמץ בפסח, ונראה שמרויחין נמי לגבי דידהו, למאי דס"ד השתא דהוי דאורייתא, דבחליפין לא אסור אלא מדרבנן, כמו שפירש בקונטרס בע"ז בפרק רבי ישמעאל (עבודה זרה דף נד:) גבי כי חרם הוא, ודריש הוא למעוטי ערלה וכלאי הכרם, שאם מכרם וקדש בדמיהם מקודשת. ופי' בקונטרס דדוקא בקדושי אשה, אבל בשאר חליפין אסור מדרבנן. ונראה שפשוט לו לרש"י דאסור מדרבנן מטעם שפירש כאן, דא"כ מצינו דמים לחמץ בפסח, ואין זה דיוקא, דאפילו יהיו הדמים מותרין כשמכרן, מ"מ כיון דלכתחלה אסור למכור לאו בר דמים הוא. ומיהו נראה שיש לאסור מדרבנן, דבנדרים פרק השותפין (נדרים דף מז:) בעי רמי בר חמא: קונם פירות הללו על פלוני מהו בחליפין? ת"ש: המקדש בערלה כו', מכרן וקדש בדמיהן מקודשת, ש"מ דחליפי איסורי הנאה מותרין. ודחי: דלמא לכתחלה הוא דלא, הא דיעבד עבד. ומיהו אע"ג דבשאר חליפין אסור, באשה שרי משום פריה ורביה, א"נ לא אסרו אלא כגון פירות וכלים שהוא דבר הניכר ונראה. וא"ת: מאי פריך בריש פרק בתרא דע"ז (דף סב.) גבי השוכר הפועל לעשות עמו יין נסך שכרו אסור, מ"ט? אילימא משום דיין נסך אסור בהנאה שכרו נמי אסור, והרי ערלה וכלאי הכרם דאסור בהנאה, ותנן מכרם וקדש בדמיהם מקודשת, ומאי קשיא? הא לכתחלה אסור ליהנות. וי"ל דמשמע ליה שכרו אסור גם לאחרים כמו יין נסך עצמו, ולהכי פריך שפיר, דאי אסור גם לאחרים כמו יין נסך אמאי מקודשת, כיון דגם היא אסורה ליהנות. ונהי דאמרינן בריש כל שעה (פסחים דף כא:) דהמקדש בשעות דרבנן וחמץ דרבנן דחוששין לקדושין, מ"מ מקודשת גמורה לא הויא, דאם בא אחר וקדשה חוששין לקידושי שניהם:
Tosafot on Chullin 4b:1:1.english: Permitted immediately, because they exchange [it] - This means: it is permitted for benefit (hana'ah) - to sell it or to feed it to gentile laborers or to dogs - but for a Jew it is forbidden to eat, since [the Sages] decreed against the bread of gentiles [by rabbinic law]. Alternatively, as Rabbeinu Tam explained, that [the mishnah] deals with dough (batzek), which is permitted to eat. And now it fits well, so that there is no difficulty [with] how did they think it follows Rabbi Yehuda - doesn't he hold, in the chapter "Kol Sha'ah" (Pesachim 28b), that chametz belonging to a gentile over which Pesach passed is forbidden for benefit? Rather, [the mishnah] deals with dough, and they exchange the dough of gentiles that was kneaded after Pesach, and "permitted immediately," which it says, means [after] the time required for kneading. And as for what Rashi explained, that they profit - that as far as we are concerned, in any case it is permitted, since it does not take hold of its proceeds [i.e., the money received for it does not become forbidden] - for specifically for him [the gentile] is it forbidden, since it came to him on account of chametz on Pesach - it also seems that they profit with regard to them [the gentiles] as well, according to what we now think, that it is a Torah prohibition, for through exchange it is forbidden only rabbinically, as Rashi explained in Avodah Zarah, in the chapter "Rabbi Yishmael" (Avodah Zarah 54b), regarding [the verse] "for it is proscribed" (ki cherem hu) - and he expounds [the word] "it" to exclude orlah and kilei hakerem [forbidden mixed plantings of a vineyard] - that if one sold them and betrothed [a woman] with their proceeds, she is betrothed. And Rashi explained there that this is specifically regarding betrothal of a woman, but regarding other exchanges it is forbidden rabbinically. And it seems obvious to Rashi that it is forbidden rabbinically, for the reason he explained here - for if it were so [that exchange were fully permitted], we would find that chametz on Pesach has monetary value. But this is not [really] a valid proof, for even if the proceeds were permitted once he sells it, nevertheless, since it is forbidden to sell it ab initio (lechatchila), it is not considered to have monetary value. However, it seems that there is reason to forbid it rabbinically, for in Nedarim, chapter "HaShutafin" (Nedarim 47b), Rami bar Chama raises the question: [If one says,] "Konam, these fruits are forbidden to so-and-so" - what is [the law] regarding exchange [of them]? Come and hear: one who betroths [a woman] with orlah, etc. - if he sold it and betrothed with its proceeds, she is betrothed; this shows that exchanging items forbidden for benefit is permitted. And [the Gemara] rejects [this]: perhaps it is only ab initio that it is not [permitted], but after the fact (bediavad) it is valid. However, even though regarding other exchanges it is forbidden, with a woman it is permitted on account of [the mitzvah of] procreation (pru u'rvu). Alternatively, they forbade it only in cases such as fruit and vessels, which are a recognizable, visible item. And if you should ask: what is the difficulty raised at the beginning of the last chapter of Avodah Zarah (62a), regarding one who hires a laborer to make wine used for idolatrous libation (yayin nesech) with him - that his wages are forbidden - what is the reason? If you say it is because yayin nesech is forbidden for benefit, so his wages are also forbidden - but there is orlah and kilei hakerem, which are forbidden for benefit, and yet we learned that if one sold them and betrothed with their proceeds, she is betrothed! So what is the difficulty? After all, it is only ab initio that it is forbidden to derive benefit [from them, while the proceeds remain permitted]! And one can answer: it seems to [the Gemara] that his wages are forbidden even to others, just like yayin nesech itself, and therefore the question is well-founded - for if his wages are forbidden to others as well, just like yayin nesech itself, why would she be betrothed, since she too would be forbidden to derive benefit from it? And granted that we say, at the beginning of "Kol Sha'ah" (Pesachim 21b), that one who betroths [a woman] with [chametz during] the rabbinically [forbidden] hours, or with rabbinically [forbidden] chametz - that we are concerned for the betrothal - nevertheless it would not be a fully valid betrothal, for if another man then comes and betroths her, we would be concerned for both betrothals [being valid].

Tosafot on Chullin 4b:5:1.hebrew: שמתו אחיו מחמת מילה - שנימולו כשהן גדולים ומתו, דאי בשמיני, דלמא משום דלא נבלע בהם הדם, כדאמר במסכת שבת (דף קלד.). א"נ אפילו בשמיני, וכגון שהציצו בהן וראו שנבלע בהן דמן:
Tosafot on Chullin 4b:5:1.english: Whose brothers died on account of circumcision - This means that they were circumcised when they were grown and [then] died. For if [the death occurred when they were circumcised] on the eighth day, perhaps it was [not due to a hereditary condition but] because their blood had not yet become absorbed [i.e., properly set], as is said in tractate Shabbat (134a). Alternatively: even if it was on the eighth day, [it could still count as proof of a hereditary condition, provided] they performed metzitzah (suction) on them and saw that their blood had become absorbed.

Tosafot on Chullin 4b:6:1.hebrew: אלא מומר לאותו דבר - ולתיאבון, דאי להכעיס פשיטא דפסולה:
Tosafot on Chullin 4b:6:1.english: Rather, an apostate with regard to that matter - meaning one who transgresses out of desire (le-teiavon), for if it were out of spite (le-hach'is), it would be obvious that [his slaughter] is invalid.

Tosafot on Chullin 4b:7:1.hebrew: מומר לעבודת כוכבים מותר לאכול משחיטתו - תימה, דבפרק בתרא דהוריות (דף יא.) פליגי בה רב אחא ורבינא במומר להכעיס, אי הוי צדוקי או מומר, אבל עובד עבודת כוכבים לכולי עלמא הוי צדוקי. ולקמן (חולין דף יג.) תני שחיטת צדוקי לעבודת כוכבי'. י"ל דצדוקי דלקמן היינו לעבודת כוכבים שעובד לכוכבים תמיד:
Tosafot on Chullin 4b:7:1.english: A mumar (apostate) to idol worship (avodat kochavim) - it is permitted to eat from his slaughter - This is astonishing (tima)! For in the last chapter of Horayot (11a), Rav Acha and Ravina disagree about a mumar le-hach'is (one who transgresses out of spite, rather than desire), as to whether he is [treated as] a tzaduki (Sadducee) or [merely] a mumar; but one who worships idols is, according to everyone, [treated as] a tzaduki. And further on (Chullin 13a) it teaches: the slaughter of a tzaduki is [invalid, being reckoned] as for idol worship. One can answer that the tzaduki spoken of further on refers to idol worship performed by one who worships idols constantly (tamid).

Rashi on Chullin 4b:11:2.english: Eating too - [This is stated] as a plain assertion, not as a question.

Rashi on Chullin 4b:12:1.hebrew: סתם יינם הוא - שלא ראינוהו שנסכו לעבודת כוכבים, דליתסר, דכתיב (דברים לב) ישתו יין נסיכם, ואפילו חשבת ליה מומר לכל התורה כולה, שרי, דעדיין לא נאסר יינם של עובדי כוכבים, דמי"ח דבר דתלמידי שמאי והלל הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 4b:12:1.english: It is wine of unknown status - [Meaning] that we have not seen him pour it as a libation to idolatry, which would render it forbidden, as it is written (Deuteronomy 32): "let them drink the wine of their libations." And even if you consider him an apostate with respect to the entire Torah, it is permitted, for the wine of idolaters had not yet been forbidden, since that is [one] of the eighteen things [enacted] by the disciples of Shammai and Hillel.

Rashi on Chullin 4b:14:1.english: He was not able to suffice - He alone was not able to suffice to slaughter for all of them.

Rashi on Chullin 4b:15:1.english: Seven thousand knees which have not bowed to Baal - This is written [in reference to the time] of Ahab.

Rashi on Chullin 4b:16:1.hebrew: גברי דאחאב - הממונים על ביתו ושוחטין לו, וכיון דהוו בבית אחאב לא הוו יראין מאיזבל, דהא עובדיה ממונה על ביתו וצדיק גמור היה:
Rashi on Chullin 4b:16:1.english: The men of Ahab - Those appointed over his household who slaughter for him. And since they were in Ahab's household, they were not afraid of Jezebel, for Obadiah was appointed over his household and was a completely righteous man.
